import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 479

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/479](https://www.erdosproblems.com/479)
-/

namespace Erdos479

/--
Is it true that, for every integer $k\neq 1$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$2^n\equiv k\pmod{n}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_479 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k : ℤ) (k ≠ 1),
    { n : ℕ | (2 : ℤ) ^ n ≡ k [ZMOD (n : ℤ)] }.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos479

reformulations.difference: The extended binder introduces an unused outer integer quantifier: the predicate elaborates to `∀ k₀ : ℤ, ∀ k : ℤ, k ≠ 1 → S(k).Infinite`. Also, the solution set ranges over all natural numbers rather than explicitly positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The unused outer quantifier can be removed by instantiating it at 0, and added by ignoring its argument. At n = 0, the congruence is equivalent to 1 = k, impossible under k ≠ 1, so all permitted solutions are already positive. Removing the trivial solution n = 1 also preserves infinitude, covering the source's nontrivial-minimum convention. In scratch.lean, I proved the complete equivalence to the single-k formulation with n > 1, retaining an arbitrary proposition in the answer position and without using the admitted problem theorem.
